chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām that Ibn Abī al-ʿAwjāʾ said to Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Aḥwal:
Why does the weak woman have one share, while the strong and wealthy man has two shares?
He said: I mentioned that to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said: “A woman has no ʿāqilah obligation, nor is maintenance upon her, nor jihad.”
And he listed other things besides this, and this is upon the man; therefore two shares were assigned to him, and one share to her.

key_terms.جِهَادٌ: jihad, a duty of armed striving assigned here to men
key_terms.عَاقِلَةٌ: the blood-money liability group or indemnity responsibility
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْأَةِ ٱلضَّعِيفَةِ: the woman described here as socially and legally less burdened in financial obligations

ai.seo_question: Why does a man receive two inheritance shares while a woman receives one in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal rationale given for the difference between the inheritance share of a man and that of a woman. It grounds that distinction in financial and social obligations placed upon men, such as maintenance and jihad, which are not assigned to women in the same way.
